partner_context.their_ambition: Merseytravel runs the cross-Mersey ferry for the Liverpool City Region — the historic link between Liverpool's Pier Head and the Wirral shore at Seacombe and Woodside. With the City Region committed to zero-carbon by 2035 and Woodside's landing stage being rebuilt, the ambition is to bring the cross-river commute back as a fast, clean public service rather than only a heritage cruise.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, foiling upgrade to a crossing Merseytravel already operates. The same terminals — Pier Head, Seacombe and Woodside — served by fast, near-silent, low-wake foiling ferries that turn a 50-minute heritage loop back into a genuine minutes-long commuter link across the Mersey.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Liverpool City Region, UK · Mersey Ferries
hero.title: Navier × Mersey Ferries — the cross-river commute, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on the Mersey crossing: fast, direct Liverpool–Wirral commutes, cleaner air, and a modern public link to sit alongside the heritage service.
hero.what_we_do_together: Merseytravel brings the cross-Mersey terminals and the public transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we turn the estuary crossing into a fast, quiet, zero-emission commuter service for the Liverpool City Region.

why_now: Liverpool City Region has committed to net zero by 2035, Seacombe is active and Woodside's landing stage is being rebuilt — an open moment to re-platform the cross-river service onto zero-emission foiling vessels as terminal works complete.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing Mersey crossing — Pier Head beside Liverpool's waterfront transport hub, Seacombe on the Wallasey shore, and Woodside at Birkenhead — taking the fast commuter runs while the heritage River Explorer service continues. Commuters step from bus and rail at Pier Head straight onto a foil across the estuary.

journeys_unlocked.label: Pier Head ↔ Seacombe
journeys_unlocked.today: The Liverpool–Wallasey commute means the road tunnels or a slow heritage loop.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The primary cross-river commute, flown clear of the water — fast, near-silent, zero-emission.

journeys_unlocked.label: Pier Head ↔ Woodside
journeys_unlocked.today: The Liverpool–Birkenhead link is a tunnel drive or a cruise, not a quick ferry.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A direct cross-river run to Woodside as its landing stage reopens — clean and quick.

journeys_unlocked.label: Seacombe ↔ Woodside
journeys_unlocked.today: The two Wirral terminals are a road trip apart along the shore.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A quiet Wirral-side water connector between Seacombe and Woodside — zero-emission.

differentiation.why_navier: Proven in service and purpose-built for this crossing: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (an advantage on a busy tidal estuary), near-silent and zero-emission. It restores a real commuter tier on the Mersey without displacing the heritage service.

proof_points.claim: Mersey Ferries is a live public service.
proof_points.evidence: Merseytravel operates the cross-Mersey ferry from Liverpool's Pier Head to Seacombe and Woodside (Woodside landing stage under refurbishment).
Liverpool City Region has committed to a zero-carbon target by 2035.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

proof_points.claim: The cross-river commute is a real gap.
proof_points.evidence: The daily commuter link is now largely a River Explorer cruise — the credible opening for a genuine fast commuter tier.

objections.concern: Can a foiling ferry work on the tidal Mersey?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at the existing terminals, flies above the estuary chop for a smoother ride, and its low wake is gentle on landing stages and the shoreline.

objections.concern: Is this affordable for a public service?
objections.response: Foiling-electric is ~10x more efficient than a diesel planing hull, so fuel — the largest operating cost — falls sharply; the same public budget runs more frequent crossings.

objections.concern: Does this end the heritage service?
objections.response: No — it's a faster layer alongside it. The River Explorer cruise continues; the foiling fleet adds a clean, fast commuter option.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path, aligned to UK MCA requirements.
the_ask.partner_brings: The cross-Mersey terminals, the public transport mandate, and the Woodside terminal-renewal timeline.
the_ask.next_step: Pick the first cross-river commuter run — most likely Pier Head–Seacombe — for a zero-emission foiling pilot, timed to Woodside's reopening.

close.body: The Mersey crossing is part of Liverpool's identity and Merseytravel runs it every day. Navier is how it becomes a fast, clean commuter link again — a quiet, zero-emission ride across the estuary that helps the City Region hit its 2035 zero-carbon goal.

end_state.headline: A zero-emission foiling layer across the Mersey cross-river network.
end_state.addressable_footprint: The cross-Mersey terminals — Pier Head, Seacombe and Woodside — re-platformed onto foiling-electric vessels.
